sections.h2: What are my choices if I want to sell a Columbia, TN house quickly?
sections.html:
You have three: accept a direct cash offer, put the house on the market with an agent, or find a buyer on your own. Cash is the quickest because nobody has to wait for a mortgage underwriter, and the buyer takes the house in its current condition.

Columbia is the county seat of Maury County, on the Duck River south of Nashville. The Census Bureau counted 41,690 residents in April 2020 and now estimates 50,072 for July 1, 2025. The city's own 2024 special census, reported on Wikipedia, found 48,885. A place that added thousands of people in a few years usually has plenty of buyers, but a house that needs a new roof or a kitchen can still sit unsold for months.

  • Cash buyer: fewest steps, no repair list, and a price that already accounts for the work.
  • Agent listing: wider exposure, with inspections, showings and buyer financing to manage.
  • Do it yourself: no commission, though pricing, disclosures and the contract fall to you.

Whichever path you pick, line up a payoff letter from your mortgage servicer and a current tax balance first.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Columbia households?
sections.html:
Columbia is a city of homeowners and long-term residents. About 63.3% of housing units are lived in by their owners, and 87.8% of people age one and older were in the same house a year earlier. The midpoint home is valued at $308,700 for 2020 to 2024, and renters pay a median of $1,197 a month.

A 28-minute average commute suggests many residents drive out of town for work, so tell buyers how far your house is from the main roads.

sections.h2: Does Columbia's history change how I should present an older house?
sections.html:
It can. Columbia was laid out in 1808, a year after Maury County was organized, and incorporated in 1817. Wikipedia calls the city and county the Antebellum Homes Capital of Tennessee and notes that Columbia holds one of the last two surviving homes of President James K. Polk. The city celebrates Mule Day every April and styles itself the mule capital of the world.

Union troops burned Jackson College and most of the town during the Civil War, so the oldest buildings that remain draw attention. If your house is from an early era, ask the city planning office whether any historic-district rules apply to your address before you tell a buyer what they may alter on the exterior.

Schooling is handled by Maury County Public Schools. Columbia State Community College, established in 1966 as Tennessee's first two-year college, has its main campus here. Private options named on Wikipedia include Columbia Academy, Zion Christian Academy and Agathos Classical School.

sections.h2: How do the river and the weather treat a Columbia house?
sections.html:
The town grew on the south bank of the Duck River at the edge of the Nashville Basin, at roughly 637 feet above sea level, with the Highland Rim climbing to the south and west. The Duck is the longest river lying wholly inside Tennessee, which is worth remembering if your lot is close to the water.

Winters are mild to cool and summers hot and humid. A weather station near Columbia records about 56.8 inches of precipitation in a normal year, with December the wettest month at 5.64 inches. July afternoons average a high near 89 degrees, and January nights average a low near 27 degrees.

  • Look at gutters, grading and the crawl space after a wet winter.
  • Ask your insurer whether the lot is in a mapped flood area.
  • Keep invoices for heating and cooling work, since both seasons are real.

sections.h2: What should a Columbia seller know about the Maury County tax bill?
sections.html:
The Maury County Trustee bills real and personal property tax each October, using the owner of record on January 1. Payment is open from the first Monday of October until the last day of February. Interest and a penalty start on March 1 at 1.5% and build every month after that, and accounts still open on April 1 move to Chancery Court.

The trustee's office, at One Public Square (931-375-2201), takes partial payments and will debit an account monthly if you ask. Paying online adds a 2.5% fee that goes to the payment vendor. Because Tennessee does not require tax notices to be mailed, a bill that never arrived is no defense against interest. The Maury County Trustee page has the full list of terms.

If the sale falls in the middle of a year, your closing company divides the bill between you and the buyer. Ask the trustee for the exact balance before you sign.

sections.h2: Why does 2026 matter for Columbia property values?
sections.html:
Maury County reappraises real estate every four years, and 2026 is a reappraisal year. The Assessor, whose office is at 6 Public Square (931-375-4001), values property as of January 1 of the reappraisal year and then adds the equalized value of improvements built later.

A bill is figured by taking the appraised value, applying the assessment ratio for the property's class, and multiplying by the rate the Maury County Commission adopts. An owner who disagrees with a value can go to the local board of equalization first and the State Board of Equalization after that. The Maury County Assessor page explains the steps.

If you are selling this year or next, tell your buyer or their lender about the new value, since the following bill may differ from what you paid before.

sections.h2: Who records the deed when a Columbia house sells?
sections.html:
The Maury County Register of Deeds records the deed. The office is a constitutional one under state law, and its stated mission includes archiving records permanently and making them viewable by the public. The county's quick links include a fee calculator for recording costs.

Tennessee's recordation tax joins a realty transfer tax with a mortgage tax. The Department of Revenue says the register collects it and sends it on, as the state recordation tax page describes.

When the house came to you from a relative, bring the probate paperwork to the closing company so it can confirm who may sign. Ask the register for the exact fee on your deed before closing day.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Columbia house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A direct buyer purchases the property in its present state and prices the needed work into the offer, so you skip contractors and open houses. Compare that net figure with what a repaired listing would bring.

faqs.q: What day does Maury County tax turn delinquent?
faqs.a: March 1. The 1.5% penalty and interest begins then and grows each month, and unpaid accounts are sent to Chancery Court on April 1.

faqs.q: Is Maury County being reappraised now?
faqs.a: Yes. The Assessor's page says reappraisals happen every four years and names 2026 as the current reappraisal year. You can appeal a value to the local board of equalization.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Maury County tax in installments?
faqs.a: The trustee takes partial payments and offers monthly bank debits, but interest applies on March 1 to any balance still unpaid.

faqs.q: Where do I get a copy of my Columbia deed?
faqs.a: Contact the Maury County Register of Deeds, which records deeds and keeps them permanently. Your closing papers may also hold a copy.
